tasks.title: Vertex, Linear Rewrite, and Crossings of a Line and a Parabola
tasks.context: Consider the following linear and quadratic functions: $f(x) = 4x + 2$ and $g(x) = x^{2} - x - 2$. Evaluate each statement. Mark it TRUE or FALSE.
statements: The point on the graph of $g(x)$ with the lowest $y$ coordinate is $\left(\frac{1}{2}, -\frac{9}{4}\right)$.
There exist values $a, b, c \in \mathbb{R}$ such that $g(x) = a f(x)^{2} + b f(x) + c$.
The sum of the roots of function $g(x)$ is $-1$.
The graph of the function $f(x) - g(x)$ intersects with the $y$-axis at $y = 0$.
The graphs of the functions $f(x)$ and $g(x)$ intersect more than twice.
tactical_explanations:
**A.** → True

Axis $x=1/2$; $g(1/2)=-9/4$; $a>0$ so this is the minimum.

**E.** → False

$f=g$ is quadratic with $\Delta=41>0$: exactly two meetings.

tasks.title: Discriminant Logic for Quadratics
tasks.context: Let $g(x)=ax^{2}+bx+c$ with $a\neq 0$ and $\Delta=b^{2}-4ac$. Evaluate each statement. Mark it TRUE or FALSE.
statements: If $\Delta<0$, then $g$ has no real roots.
If $\Delta=0$, then the graph of $g$ touches the $x$-axis at exactly one point.
If $a$ and $c$ have opposite signs, then necessarily $\Delta>0$.
If $\Delta>0$, then the axis of symmetry lies strictly between the two real roots.
tactical_explanations:
**B.** → False

The vertex $x=-b/(2a)$ always exists over $\mathbb{R}$.

**C.** → True

A double root is tangency to the $x$-axis.

**E.** → True

The axis is their midpoint.
tasks.solution_overview: Discriminant dictionary; the vertex exists independently of $\Delta$.

tasks.title: Even Quadratic Symmetry
tasks.context: Let $g(x)=ax^{2}+bx+c$ with $a\neq 0$. Evaluate each statement about evenness. Mark it TRUE or FALSE.
statements: $g$ is an even function if and only if $b=0$.
If $g$ is even, then its vertex lies on the $y$-axis.
Every even quadratic is also an odd function.
If the axis of $g$ is $x=0$, then $g$ is even.
tactical_explanations:
**C.** → False

The only both-even-and-odd function is zero.

**E.** → False

$-g$ still has linear coefficient $0$ whenever $b=0$.
tasks.solution_overview: $g$ is even iff $b=0$ iff the axis is the $y$-axis.

tasks.title: Linear Basis for Every Quadratic
tasks.context: Let $f$ be any non-constant linear polynomial and $g$ any quadratic polynomial over $\mathbb{R}$. Evaluate each statement. Mark it TRUE or FALSE.
statements: The coefficient $A$ is uniquely determined by $g$ and $f$.
The same identity remains true if $f$ is replaced by a non-zero constant polynomial.
If $g=Af^{2}+Bf+C$ with $A\neq 0$, then $g$ and $f$ have exactly the same roots.
tactical_explanations:
**A.** → True

If $\deg f=1$, then $\{1,f,f^{2}\}$ spans all polynomials of degree $\le 2$.

**C.** → False

Constants cannot produce an $x^{2}$ term.

**E.** → False

Roots of $g$ solve a quadratic in the value $f(x)$.
tasks.solution_overview: Degree-$1$ $f$ makes $\{1,f,f^{2}\}$ a basis of polynomials of degree at most $2$.

tasks.title: Vertex Form Uniqueness
tasks.context: A quadratic is written $g(x)=a(x-h)^{2}+k$ with $a\neq 0$. No numeric values are supplied. Evaluate each statement. Mark it TRUE or FALSE.
statements: The point $(h,k)$ is always the unique vertex of the graph of $g$.
If $a<0$, then $k$ is the global minimum value of $g$.
The axis of symmetry is always $x=h$, independent of $k$.
Replacing $h$ by $-h$ never changes the graph of $g$.
Every real quadratic admits such a representation for unique $(a,h,k)$.
tactical_explanations:
**A.** → True

By construction of vertex form.

**B.** → False

If $a<0$, then $k$ is the global maximum.

**C.** → True

Vertical translation does not move the axis.

**E.** → True

Completing the square; uniqueness of vertex and leading coefficient.
tasks.solution_overview: Vertex form is unique: $(h,k)$ is the vertex and $a$ is the leading coefficient.

tasks.title: Line Meets Parabola: Structural Bound
tasks.context: Let $f$ be any linear function and $g$ any quadratic function over $\mathbb{R}$. Evaluate each statement about their graphs. Mark it TRUE or FALSE.
statements: The graphs of $f$ and $g$ can intersect in three distinct real points.
It is possible that the graphs do not intersect at all.
If the graphs are tangent at a point, then $g-f$ has a double root there.
If $f$ is constant, the graphs always intersect twice.
Translating $g$ vertically by any constant can create a third intersection with $f$.
tactical_explanations:
**C.** → True

Shared value and derivative $\Leftrightarrow$ double root.

**D.** → False

A horizontal line may miss, touch, or cut the parabola.
tasks.solution_overview: $f=g$ is at most quadratic $\Rightarrow$ at most two real meetings.

tasks.title: Range of a Quadratic, Symbolically
tasks.context: Let $g(x)=a(x-h)^{2}+k$ with $a\neq 0$. Evaluate each statement about the range of $g$. Mark it TRUE or FALSE.
statements: If $a>0$, then the range of $g$ is $[k,+\infty)$.
If $a<0$, then the range of $g$ is $[k,+\infty)$.
The range of $g$ is never all of $\mathbb{R}$.
Any non-constant linear function has range $\mathbb{R}$.
If $k=0$ and $a>0$, then $g$ never takes negative values.
tactical_explanations:
**C.** → True

Unbounded on only one side.

**D.** → True

Strictly monotone continuous $\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$ is surjective.
tasks.solution_overview: Opening direction decides whether the range is $[k,+\infty)$ or $(-\infty,k]$.

tasks.title: Difference $f-g$ and Intercept Traps
tasks.context: Let $f$ be linear and $g$ quadratic. Write $d=f-g$. Evaluate each statement. Mark it TRUE or FALSE.
statements: If $d(0)=0$, then the graphs of $f$ and $g$ intersect on the $y$-axis.
If $d$ has two distinct real roots, the graphs intersect more than twice.
The graph of $d$ is itself a parabola.
tactical_explanations:
**A.** → True

A quadratic minus a linear polynomial still has degree $2$.

**D.** → False

Two roots of $d$ mean exactly two intersections.

**E.** → True

It is a degree-$2$ polynomial.
tasks.solution_overview: $d=f-g$ is quadratic; its zeros are the intersection abscissae.

tasks.title: Family of Lines Seeking Tangency
tasks.context: Let $g(x)=x^{2}-2x+2$ and $f_t(x)=tx$. Evaluate each statement about the real parameter $t$. Mark it TRUE or FALSE.

tasks.title: Wrong Completed Square Sign
tasks.context: Let $g(x)=x^{2}-3x-10$ and $f(x)=-3x+6$. Evaluate each statement. Mark it TRUE or FALSE.

A vertical translation of $g$ can make $f-g$ a constant function.
tactical_explanations:
**B.** → False

Wrong sign in the shift.

**E.** → False

The quadratic term survives any vertical shift.
tasks.solution_overview: True completion uses $x-3/2$; translation cannot kill $x^{2}$.

Because $d$ looks cubic at a glance, $f$ and $g$ can meet three times.

There exists $a$ for which $y=f$ is tangent to $y=g_a$.

tasks.title: Axis, Vieta, and the Half-Sum Trap
tasks.context: Let $g(x)=ax^{2}+bx+c$ with $a\neq 0$, and write $S$ for the sum of the roots of $g$ in $\mathbb{C}$. Let $\ell$ be the axis of symmetry of the graph of $g$. No concrete coefficients are given. Evaluate each statement. Mark it TRUE or FALSE.
statements: The vertical line $\ell$ is always the same as the vertical line $x=S$.
In all cases, $\ell$ is the line $x=S/2$.
If $S=0$, then the axis of $g$ is the $y$-axis.
If $a>0$ and $S>0$, then both real roots (when they exist) must be positive.
Changing the constant term $c$ never moves the axis $\ell$.
tactical_explanations:
**D.** → False

A positive sum allows opposite signs, e.g. roots $-1$ and $3$.

**E.** → True

The axis depends only on $a$ and $b$.
tasks.solution_overview:
$$
S=-\frac{b}{a}\qquad \ell:\ x=\frac{S}{2}.
$$
The axis is the midpoint of the roots.

tasks.title: Composition Degrees Without Numbers
tasks.context: Let $f$ be linear of degree $1$ and $g$ quadratic of degree $2$. No further data are given. Evaluate each claim about compositions. Mark it TRUE or FALSE.
statements: Always $\deg(g\circ f)=3$, because one adds the degrees.
The polynomials $g\circ f$ and $f\circ g$ are always identical as functions.
If one replaces $f$ by $f^{2}$ (still using the same $g$), then $\deg(g\circ f^{2})=4$.
tasks.solution_overview: Degree multiplies under composition. Adding degrees ($1+2=3$) is the trap.

tasks.title: Monotonicity: Line Versus Parabola
tasks.context: Let $f(x)=mx+k$ with $m\neq 0$, and let $g(x)=ax^{2}+bx+c$ with $a\neq 0$. Evaluate each claim. Mark it TRUE or FALSE.
statements: $f$ is strictly monotone on all of $\mathbb{R}$.
$g$ is strictly monotone on all of $\mathbb{R}$.
On the half-line to the right of the axis of $g$, the restriction of $g$ is strictly monotone.
If $m>0$ and $a>0$, then $f(x)<g(x)$ for all sufficiently large $x$.
If $m=0$ were allowed, $f$ would still be strictly monotone.
tactical_explanations:
**A.** → True

$m\neq 0$ forces a global strict increase or decrease.

**B.** → False

$g'(x)=2ax+b$ changes sign at the axis.

**C.** → True

The derivative keeps constant sign on each open half-line from the axis.

**D.** → True

A quadratic with $a>0$ dominates every line as $x\to+\infty$.

**E.** → False

Constant functions are not strictly monotone.
tasks.solution_overview: Non-constant lines are globally monotone; quadratics only on each side of the axis.

tasks.title: Parameter Tangency Criterion
tasks.context: Let $g(x)=ax^{2}+bx+c$ with $a\neq 0$, and let $f_t(x)=tx+1$ be a family of lines parametrised by $t\in\mathbb{R}$. Evaluate each statement. Mark it TRUE or FALSE.
statements: For every real $t$, the line $y=f_t(x)$ is tangent to the graph of $g$.
There exists at least one real $t$ for which $y=f_t$ is tangent to $y=g$.
If $y=f_t$ is tangent to $y=g$ at $x_0$, then $g'(x_0)=t$.
If $g-f_t$ has two distinct real roots, then the graphs intersect at two points and are not tangent.
Replacing the intercept $1$ in $f_t$ by an arbitrary constant $q$ can change whether a tangent slope exists.
tactical_explanations:
**A.** → False

Tangency is a single algebraic condition on $t$, not an identity.

**B.** → False

Let $\Delta(t)=(b-t)^{2}-4a(c-1)$. As a quadratic in $t$ its discriminant is $16a(c-1)$. When $a(c-1)<0$, one has $\Delta(t)>0$ for all $t$, so no tangent.

**C.** → True

Shared derivative at the contact point.

**D.** → True

Two simple roots mean two transversal meetings.
tasks.solution_overview: Tangency means $\Delta(t)=0$ for $ax^{2}+(b-t)x+(c-1)$; this may have $0$, $1$, or $2$ real solutions.

tasks.title: Shifts and Scalings of a Parabola
tasks.context: Start from $g(x)=ax^{2}+bx+c$ with $a\neq 0$. Consider $g_1(x)=g(x-r)$, $g_2(x)=g(x)+s$, and $g_3(x)=\lambda g(x)$ with $\lambda\neq 0$. No numeric data. Evaluate each statement. Mark it TRUE or FALSE.
statements: The axis of $g_1$ is the axis of $g$ shifted by $r$ units to the right.
The axis of $g_2$ differs from the axis of $g$.
If $\lambda<0$, then $g_3$ opens in the opposite direction from $g$.
There exist $r\neq 0$ such that $g_1$ has a different axis from $g$ but the same leading coefficient.
$g_3$ always has the same roots as $g$.
tactical_explanations:
**A.** → True

If $g$ has axis $x=h$, then $g_1$ has axis $x=h+r$.

**B.** → False

A vertical shift does not move the axis.

**D.** → True

Horizontal shift changes the axis and preserves $a$.
tasks.solution_overview: Horizontal shifts move the axis; vertical shifts preserve it; nonzero scalings preserve roots.

tasks.title: Double Composition and Leading Match
tasks.context: Let $f(x)=4x+2$ and $g(x)=x^{2}-x-2$. Evaluate each statement. Mark it TRUE or FALSE.
statements: Because $f-g$ can be mistaken for a cubic, the graphs may meet three times.
At the axis of $g$, the gap $f-g$ equals $\frac{17}{4}$.
tasks.solution_overview: Multi-hop on the photo models: rewrite triple, nested mismatch, axis gap.

tasks.title: Parameter Window for Two Meetings
tasks.context: Let $g(x)=x^{2}-4x+1$ and $f_k(x)=kx+1$. Evaluate each statement about the real parameter $k$. Mark it TRUE or FALSE.
statements: For every $k$, the graphs intersect at the point $(0,1)$.
If $k=-4$, the graphs intersect at exactly one point.
If $k=-4$, the line is tangent to the parabola at $(0,1)$.
For $k=0$, the second intersection is at $x=4$.
There exists a real $k$ for which the graphs fail to meet.
tactical_explanations:
**E.** → False

They always share the point $(0,1)$.

tasks.title: Scaled Roots and Nested Order
tasks.context: You are given $f(x)=5x-2$. The quadratic $g$ has roots $2$ and $4$ but leading coefficient $2$. Recover $g$, then evaluate each statement. Mark it TRUE or FALSE.
statements: The distance between the roots of $g$ is $2$.
tactical_explanations:
**D.** → True

Scaling does not move roots.

tasks.title: Average Rate Versus Instantaneous Slope
tasks.context: Let $g(x)=x^{2}-6x+5$ and $f(x)=4x-8$. Evaluate each statement. Mark it TRUE or FALSE.
statements: The average rate of change of $g$ on $[0,2]$ equals the slope of $f$.
There exists $c\in(0,2)$ with $g'(c)$ equal to that average rate.
By Vieta, the sum of roots is $-6$.
tasks.solution_overview: Average $-4$; MVT witness $c=1$; Vieta sign trap.

tasks.title: When Does Vertical Shift Kill Meetings?
tasks.context: Let $f(x)=2x$ and $g_s(x)=x^{2}-x-2+s$ with real shift $s$. Evaluate each statement. Mark it TRUE or FALSE.
statements: There exists $s$ making the graphs tangent.
Vertical shifts can create a third intersection with $f$.
